Hon'ble Subhash Vidyarthi,J.
1.
Heard Sri Mohammad Imaran, learned counsel for the applicant, Sri S.N. Goswamy, learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the records.

2. The instant application has been filed seeking release of the applicant on bail in Case Crime No.
312 of 2021, under Sections 363/366/376 (3) I.P.C. and Section 5/6 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012, registered at Police Station Jagatpur, District Raebareli.
3.

entities.text: Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: The aforesaid case has been registered on the basis of an F.I.R. lodged on 23.10.2021 against accused (i) Ankit, (ii) Ramji & (iii) Intjaar Ali, stating that the accused persons had enticed away the informant's daughter aged about 21 years and another girl aged about 13 years.
The younger victim had taken away gold ear rings, mangalsutra and anklets with her.
4. In the statement of the elder of the victims, she stated that she knows the co-accused Ankit for the past five years and she had planned to go with him.
The younger girl who is her cousin also went with them.
All three of them went to Faridabad where they stayed in a room and the applicant used to visit the said room.
The younger victim disclosed her aged to be 15 years and she stated that she Intjaar Ali vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home ...

1 knows the applicant for the past 2-3 months; that the applicant came to her house about one month ago and committed the misdeed with her and he repeated the same thing after 2-3 days.
She further stated that the applicant committed the misdeed with her at Faridabad also.
5. The victim was taken for medico legal examination and she has given similar statement to the doctor also.
Although no fresh injuries were found during her medico legal examination, but hymen has been reported to be torn.
Even in the radiological examination, the age of the younger victim has been found to be 16 years and therefore undisputedly she is a minor.

6. The State has filed a counter affidavit annexing therewith the copies of materials collected during investigation, including the statements recorded, medico legal examination report and the educational certificate of the victim, as per which her date of birth is 04.05.2007.

7. The rejoinder affidavit has been filed on behalf of the applicant, stating that the applicant was a candidate in B.D.C. Election of Nagar Panchayat Melthuwa and contested election against one Ram Sumer Pal, who was supported by Ramesh Maurya and the applicant lost election.

entities.text: B.D.C. Election of Nagar Panchayat Melthuwa
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: It has been stated in the rejoinder affidavit that Ram Sumer Pal and Ramesh Maurya belong to the same village and the applicant's mother was also elected as B.D.C. in the year 2015-16.
It has been stated that the applicant has been implicated in the present case because of the aforesaid political rivalry.

8. It has further been disclosed in the rejoinder affidavit that the applicant is involved in another case bearing Case Crime No.69 of 2018, under Section 363/366/376 I.P.C. and Section 3/4 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012, Police Station Bhadokhar, District Raebareli in which he has been enlarged on bail by this Court by means of order dated 20.07.2018, passed in Bail Application No.5900 of 2018.

entities.text: Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: It is recorded in the aforesaid bail order that the accused person had enticed away a minor girl and the applicant had taken her away to Meerut and had kept her with him for five days.
9. A supplementary affidavit has been filed on behalf of the applicant annexing therewith copies of statements recorded by learned trial court.

The informant has stated in her examination-in-chief that the younger one of the two victims had taken away some jewellery along with her to the applicant and she identified her signatures on the complaint on the basis whereof the F.I.R. was lodged.
10. The victim stated in her statement recorded before learned trial court that she knew the applicant since before and she used to talk to him.
The applicant had made physical relations with her under a false promise to marry her.

She stated that she had given the statement to the police and had also told about the incident to the doctor who had conducted her medico legal examination and she identified the statement given by her before the Magistrate.
She stated that after coming back from Faridabad she had told about the incident to her parents.
However, there are some discrepancies in her statements given in her cross-examination.
11. Learned counsel for the applicant has submitted that the victim has changed her version in her statements recorded at different stages.

2 12. Having considered the facts and circumstances of the case as also submissions advanced by learned counsel for the applicant and learned A.G.A. and from the material placed before the Court,
at this stage, there appears to be no reason to doubt that the victim is a minor.
The applicant is a person aged about 33 years and he is more than double age of the victim.

Although the victim stated that she had gone with the co-accused Ankit to the room provided by the applicant at Faridabad, she has also stated that the applicant had made physical relations with her on more than one occasion at her village as also at Faridabad.
13. Learned counsel for the applicant has submitted that the relationship was made with consent of the victim.
As has already observed above, since the victim is aged about 16 years and as per her educational certificate her age is merely 14 years and five months, her consent is immaterial.

14. Keeping in view the aforesaid facts coupled with the fact that earlier also the applicant was involved in similar incident and he had given effect to the present incident after being released on bail in the earlier case namely Case Crime No.69 of 2018, under Sections 363, 366, 376 I.P.C. and Section 3/4 Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012, the applicant has again indulged in commission of similar offence while he is granted bail, this court is not inclined to exercise its discretionary jurisdiction by enlarging the applicant on bail.

entities.text: Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 15. The bail application is accordingly dismissed.

. 
(Subhash Vidyarthi, J.) Order Date :- 21.4.2023

Ram.
